messages.text:
Good morning,

I recently purchased a pack of 3 DC06s from the site and was getting the
expected Hashrate.  I saw there were a couple firmware updates posted for
that model and went with the upgrade.  Once upgraded I have not had an
acceptable hashrate since.  I am trying to get back to ThorOS 2.0 but I
cannot find the BIN anywhere.  Can you help me get back to functioning?

Thank you,
Matthew D.

Good morning Matthew,

Thanks for the clear description. I can see why you want to get back to the version that was working.

I looked for the ThorOS 2.0 file and couldn't find it either. Hammer's official DC06 firmware page on GitHub only lists one public release,
V3.0.0-20260916, published 18 Sep
. They don't seem to publish older builds like 2.0 there. Please don't use a .bin from a forum or another unofficial source. The wrong image, or a build made for a different Hammer model, can leave a unit that looks like it's working but returns no shares. Unofficial firmware can also affect your warranty.

I've passed this to JD, our hardware lead, along with everything you described. He'll take it from here and reply in this thread. He can confirm whether we can get you the official ThorOS 2.0 image for the DC06 and how to flash it back safely.

It would help JD if you could reply with the following. First, the firmware version each of the three units shows now. Second, which update or updates you installed and where you downloaded them. Third, the hashrate each unit showed before the update and what it shows now. For the new numbers, please give both the miner's own screen or web page and your pool's figure over a few hours. Fourth, which pool you're mining on. A screenshot of the status page for one unit would also help.

There's one thing you could check in the meantime. Firmware updates sometimes reset a unit's performance mode, frequency or pool settings to defaults. Have a look at each unit's settings page and see whether anything changed from what you had before.

If you'd like a faster answer, our Discord is the quickest route: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Mention @nullhashrate (that's JD). He and the community are very active there.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

and the Official G..  I've attached what I can based on

Hi Matthew,

Thanks for the screenshots. Only three came through on my side: the firmware page twice and one NORN OS dashboard. The log images didn't arrive.

On the firmware page, the unit shows model DC06 running 3.0.0 20260916, and it's offering V3.0.1-20261012 as an update. "Preserve User Data" is ticked.

The dashboard shows the unit hashing at 4.65 MH/s right now, with a 28.2 MH/s average over 13 hours 49 minutes of uptime. The 15-minute chart sits close to zero the whole time. The unit is drawing 60 W from 12.1 V. It shows the ASIC frequency at 2300 MHz and HB1 Voltage at 3 V. The board is at 49.1°C, the VRM is at 63.3°C and the fan is at 79% (2363 RPM). The pool has accepted 3,645 shares and rejected 21 (99.43% accepted), and Wi-Fi is good at -67 dBm.

So the unit isn't overheating, isn't losing power and isn't dropping off the network. Shares are reaching the pool and nearly all are accepted. The problem is simply the hashrate, which is far below what the unit should do. A DC06 is
rated at 330 MH/s of performance while using only about 105 watts
. All three units dropped right after the update, so I suspect firmware settings rather than three faulty boards, but I can't confirm that yet. I also won't guess what the frequency and voltage on that dashboard should read under this firmware.

Here is one test to try on just one unit, so the other two stay as they are. On the Firmware Update page, untick "Preserve User Data." Then use Browse to load the official V3.0.1-20261012 .bin from Hammer's GitHub. Keeping user data may have carried old settings from ThorOS 2.0 into the new firmware, and a clean install rules that out. The unit will forget its Wi-Fi and pool settings, so you'll need to set it up again the same way you did when it was new. Leave it running at least an hour and note the hashrate on the dashboard and at your pool.

Whatever that test shows, please send me the following in your reply:

1. Whether the test unit improved.
2. A screenshot of the Settings page on one of the untouched units, showing whatever frequency, voltage or performance mode options it has.
3. The logs again, copied and pasted as text if you can, since the images didn't make it.
4. Whether all three units show the same low numbers.
5. Which pool you're mining on.

JD, our hardware lead, already has your case, including your question about getting back to ThorOS 2.0. Everything above will help him find the cause quickly. If you'd like a faster answer, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Mention @nullhashrate (JD), as he and the community are very active there.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Thank you Hal.  I will try this when I get home tonight since the unit will
likely lose WiFi I won't be able to get information from work but I will
provide as soon as I can.

Thank you,
Matt

Hi Matt,

Thanks, tonight is fine, and you're right that you'll need to be in front of the unit for this.

Two things will save you time. First, write down your Wi-Fi details and your pool URL, worker name and pool password before you flash. That way it takes a minute to set the unit up again afterwards. Second, only flash one unit and leave the other two as they are. If the clean install doesn't help, those two will still show the problem as it is now, which JD can compare against.

When you have results, just reply here with the hashrate after about an hour, the Settings page screenshot and the logs as text. JD already has your case and will see what you send.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hi Matt,

Thanks for testing that tonight, and sorry it didn't change anything. Your Wi-Fi and pools staying after a flash with "Preserve User Data" unticked is useful to know. It means that update screen isn't doing a full wipe on these units, so a proper full flash is the next step.

I've passed everything you found to JD, our hardware lead, with all the details: what the dashboard shows, the reflash that kept your settings, and the web flasher failing to connect on all three units. The team is offline for the night. Someone will pick this up tomorrow from 10am ET and reply in this thread.

If you have time before then, a few checks on the web flasher might get it connecting.

First, Firefox can't run this kind of flasher at all, because browser flashers need a feature called Web Serial that only Chrome and Edge have. So Firefox failing tells us nothing; Edge is the one that counts.

Second, the USB cable. Many cables only carry power, not data, and a power-only cable gives exactly this "can't connect" result. Try a different cable you know transfers data, plugged straight into the computer rather than through a hub.

Third, on Windows, open Device Manager and look under "Ports (COM & LPT)" as you plug the unit in. Tell me whether a new COM port appears. If nothing appears at all, the computer isn't seeing the unit. That points to the cable or a missing USB driver rather than the flasher itself.

When you reply, please include the exact error the flasher shows, if any. Please also send the logs as pasted text and a screenshot of the Settings page, since those didn't come through last time. That gives JD everything in one place.

For a quicker answer from JD directly, the Discord is https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Mention @nullhashrate there.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
